answer: For a pigment co-op voting on quarrying a crystal-rich ledge, I propose one identity per certified secure chip. Each chip runs 60 hours of fixed work monthly with a nonexportable key. The registry checks signed attestations of code, runtime, chip ID and month, and permits one identity per chip per month. Supporting n identities needs n chips and 60n chip-hours monthly; proofs cannot be reused across identities. Missing or invalid proof blocks voting. Certification and secure timers must be trusted: hacked chips can fake work, and rich buyers can still buy many identities.
